description: A grey-templed man in a long charcoal coat cut loose over whatever he's carrying, mirrored lenses on indoors, hands folded at his belt buckle. He stands on a patch of marble worn grey by eleven years of him. When you cross the hall his head turns at the speed of the cornice camera.

bye.text: The doors have him again. You have already stopped existing.

guns.text: "Everyone asks." The lenses don't move. "Yes. Licensed, insured, and logged with the precinct next door, which took the Compound four years and a great deal of money." A pause with nothing in it. "Nobody has made me open the coat since the second year. I'd rather it stayed a rumour. Rumours don't have to be reloaded."

police.text: "They're forty metres that way and they answer the phone." He tips his chin a fraction toward the east wall. "Our cameras run on their network. Their evidence locker banks with us. It's not a friendship, it's plumbing, but it means anything that happens in this hall is already happening at Precinct 9 as well, just slightly later and with worse lighting."

options.label: "How does this work with the cops next door?"

root.text: The lenses come round and hold on you a beat past comfortable. "Terminals are in the alcoves. The machine will answer anything you've got." His hands stay folded. "I'm not here for questions, but I'll take a couple if you're going to stand there anyway."

rules.text: "Two," he says. "Don't run in the hall. Don't stand still in the hall." He lets that sit. "One of those tells me you've done something. The other tells me you're about to. Walk in, do your business, walk out, and I'll forget your face by the time the door shuts. That's the service I'm actually providing."

where.text:
His hands stay folded. "Terminals in the alcoves, for pocket money. They move twenty-five hundred a day each way and not a credit more. For more than that, you ask the machine behind the counter."

"North is the vestibule, and the box gallery past it. The arch reads you on the way in. If you're wanted, you're turned round. If you're carrying contraband you'll need a story, and if the story doesn't hold, you're arrested."

clothing_layers: a long charcoal coat cut generously through the chest
a pressed white shirt and a Compound-orange tie clip
a concealment rig, worn smooth at the strap
